due_when.clears_when: compute_router routes an uncovered fetch unit to github_runner without a hand-written why_runner, with a test, or the manager records why not

origin.rerun: python3 -c "import yaml,sys; sys.path[:0]=[\".\",\"scripts/research\"]; import candle_dataset as cd; print(cd.covers(yaml.safe_load(open(\"research/queue/RQ-20261119-8260-02.yaml\"))))"   # False means the dataset cannot serve it

what: Router default sends an exit_lever_ablation unit to the no-internet Kaggle kernel when the candle dataset does not cover its fetch and the unit has no routing.why_runner. MEASURED 2026-11-19: 8260-02 (BTC 5m, --days 2610) and 8260-03 (SOL 15m, --days 2290) ran on Kaggle and failed with a DNS error on data.binance.vision; candle_dataset.covers() was False for both (days_built 1830 < days). Runner pins added by hand in the PR for those two units. The same shape cost the four mgc_15m units 11 failed runs (yfinance, a separate cause, fixed by the dukascopy flag). Proposed fix: in compute_router.runner_only_reason, treat a unit for which candle_dataset.unit_feed() returns a feed and covers() is False as runner-only without needing why_runner; covers() stays the single source. Not a gate: it removes a guaranteed failure and sends the unit to a backend that can run it.
